steps.instructions: Run standard operator-accessible readiness or self-test checks. Review printed or displayed results for ECG-related failures or repeated critical hardware messages.

CCR.Complaint: User reported ZOLL R Series displaying ECG DISABLED. ECG monitoring unavailable during startup/use. Device removed from clinical area for evaluation.
CCR.Cause: Verified ECG DISABLED message. Known-good ECG cable, lead set, simulator connection, pads monitoring check, power source, and accessory checks did not clear the error. Condition consistent with persistent ECG hardware failure involving the ECG module or analog board path.
CCR.Resolution: Removed defibrillator from service and labeled Out of Service. Sent for repair/bench evaluation for suspected analog board or ECG hardware failure. Device not returned to patient use.

title: ZOLL R Series Defibrillator - Error: ECG FAULT 7
description: Troubleshooting guide for ECG FAULT 7 on the ZOLL R Series defibrillator, indicating the ECG processor is not responding and ECG monitoring may be unavailable or unreliable.

steps.title: Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Remove the ZOLL R Series from patient use if ECG monitoring is unavailable, unreliable, frozen, or showing ECG FAULT 7. Use another defibrillator, bedside monitor, or transport monitor for active patient monitoring.

steps.title: Verify the Reported Error and Behavior
steps.instructions: Confirm the displayed message is ECG FAULT 7 and document whether it appears at startup, during self-test, when ECG leads are connected, during monitoring, or intermittently during use.

steps.title: Check Power Source and Startup Condition
steps.instructions: Connect the unit to known-good AC power, confirm battery status, install a known-good charged battery if needed, and restart the unit to see whether the fault returns.

steps.title: Perform a Controlled Restart
steps.instructions: Turn the unit off, disconnect ECG accessories, wait briefly, then power the unit back on using AC power and a known-good battery. Watch for ECG FAULT 7 during startup.

steps.title: Inspect the ECG Cable and Connector
steps.instructions: Inspect the ECG cable and ECG input connector for bent pins, cracked connectors, broken strain relief, fluid contamination, loose fit, damaged wires, debris, corrosion, or visible damage.

steps.title: Test with a Known-Good ECG Cable
steps.instructions: Install a known-good compatible ZOLL R Series ECG cable and test with an ECG simulator if available. If the waveform returns and the fault clears, replace the defective ECG cable.

steps.title: Check ECG Lead Configuration and Accessory Setup
steps.instructions: Confirm the selected ECG source matches the connected accessory and verify that leads, pads, paddles, electrodes, snaps, and lead wires are configured correctly.

steps.title: Check for Physical Damage or Contamination
steps.instructions: Inspect the unit for cracked housing, evidence of a drop, fluid intrusion, corrosion, damage around the ECG input area, loose connectors, burning smell, or abnormal heat.

steps.title: Confirm Whether the Fault Follows the Accessory or Stays with the Device
steps.instructions: Test the suspect ECG cable on another compatible unit if available and test the affected defibrillator with a known-good cable and ECG simulator. If the fault stays with the defibrillator, suspect internal ECG hardware failure.

steps.title: Determine if the Error Is Persistent
steps.instructions: After external checks, power cycle the unit again. If ECG FAULT 7 persists, remove the device from service and send it for bench evaluation, approved repair, or vendor service. The manual-indicated technical action is replacement of the analog board.

CCR.Complaint: ZOLL R Series defibrillator reported ECG FAULT 7. Staff stated ECG monitoring was unavailable and no reliable ECG waveform was displayed during use.
CCR.Cause: Verified ECG FAULT 7 on startup. Known-good AC power, charged battery, restart, ECG cable replacement, ECG simulator, and lead setup checks did not clear the fault. Persistent error indicates ECG processor not responding, likely internal analog board failure.
CCR.Resolution: Removed device from service and labeled Out of Service. Sent for bench repair or vendor evaluation for suspected analog board failure. Unit not returned to service pending repair and functional verification.

title: ZOLL R Series Defibrillator - Error: ECG FAULT 200
description: Troubleshooting guide for ECG FAULT 200 on the ZOLL R Series defibrillator, where the ECG application is unavailable and ECG monitoring or normal readiness may be affected.

steps.title: Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Remove the ZOLL R Series from patient use if ECG monitoring, pacing, cardioversion, or defibrillation readiness is affected. Transfer the patient to another monitor/defibrillator if active monitoring or therapy is needed.

steps.title: Verify the Reported Error and Behavior
steps.instructions: Power the unit on and confirm the exact displayed message is ECG FAULT 200. Note whether the error appears at startup, in ECG monitoring, during lead selection, after self-test, or intermittently during use.

steps.title: Check ECG Cable and Lead Setup First
steps.instructions: Inspect the ECG trunk cable and lead wires for bent pins, cracked connectors, contamination, fluid intrusion, or damaged insulation. Reconnect securely and test with a known-good ECG cable and lead set if available.

steps.title: Check Electrodes and Simulator Input
steps.instructions: Use a known-good ECG simulator or fresh electrodes if available. Confirm whether an ECG waveform appears and whether lead selection is possible.

steps.title: Restart the Device
steps.instructions: Power the unit off, disconnect external power, remove the battery if appropriate, wait briefly, then reinstall the battery, reconnect AC power, and restart the unit. Observe whether the ECG application becomes available.

steps.title: Check Battery and AC Power Stability
steps.instructions: Connect the device to a known-good AC outlet, verify AC power indication, install a known-good battery if available, and restart the unit using stable power.

steps.title: Check for Recent Software, Service, or Configuration Changes
steps.instructions: Determine whether the fault appeared after software loading, configuration changes, main board replacement, MCU-related service, failed software update, unexpected shutdown during update, or battery depletion during service.

steps.title: Do Not Treat This Like a Simple ECG Lead Failure
steps.instructions: After basic external checks are complete, do not continue swapping electrodes, pads, or cables if the error remains. Treat ECG FAULT 200 as an ECG application availability issue.

steps.title: Escalate for Software Reload
steps.instructions: If ECG FAULT 200 remains after restart, power checks, and basic ECG accessory checks, remove the device from service, label it Out of Service, and send it for bench evaluation or approved software reload.

CCR.Complaint: ZOLL R Series defibrillator displayed ECG FAULT 200 at startup. ECG monitoring function was unavailable and device could not be confirmed ready for patient use.
CCR.Cause: External ECG cable, lead set, power source, and restart checks did not clear the fault. Error indicated no ECG application available, consistent with software or application loading issue.
CCR.Resolution: Removed device from service and labeled Out of Service. Sent for bench evaluation and approved reload of MCU software and ECG application software. Device not returned to service pending repair and operational verification.

title: ZOLL R Series Defibrillator - Error: CHECK ECG CABLE
description: Troubleshooting guide for CHECK ECG CABLE errors on the ZOLL R Series defibrillator, including ECG cable connection checks, source selection, leadwire inspection, known-good cable testing, ECG simulator verification, and service escalation.

steps.title: Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Remove the device from patient use if ECG monitoring is unreliable. Transfer the patient to another monitor or defibrillator if continuous ECG monitoring or therapy capability is needed.

steps.title: Verify the Reported Error and Behavior
steps.instructions: Confirm the display reads CHECK ECG CABLE and document whether it appears at startup, during ECG monitoring, when the cable is moved, or intermittently during use.

steps.title: Confirm the Correct ECG Source Is Selected
steps.instructions: Verify the selected ECG source matches the connected accessory, such as ECG cable, pads, or paddles.

steps.title: Inspect the ECG Cable Connection at the Device
steps.instructions: Disconnect and inspect the ECG connector for bent pins, loose fit, cracked housing, contamination, fluid residue, damaged locking tabs, or worn connector hardware.

steps.title: Inspect the ECG Cable and Leadwires
steps.instructions: Check the ECG trunk cable and leadwires for cuts, kinks, pinched sections, exposed conductors, broken strain relief, loose connections, corrosion, or residue.

steps.title: Replace the ECG Cable With a Known-Good Cable
steps.instructions: Install a known-good compatible ZOLL R Series ECG cable and check whether the CHECK ECG CABLE message clears.

steps.title: Check the Electrodes and Patient Lead Connections
steps.instructions: Use fresh electrodes, confirm proper adhesion, check leadwire placement, and verify secure snap or clip connections.

steps.title: Check for Contamination or Cleaning Damage
steps.instructions: Inspect the ECG port and cable connector for moisture, cleaning fluid residue, corrosion, sticky residue, or visible fluid intrusion.

steps.title: Test ECG Monitoring Function
steps.instructions: Connect the device to an ECG simulator using a known-good ECG cable and confirm stable waveform, heart rate display, proper lead selection, and no CHECK ECG CABLE message.

steps.title: Determine Whether the Issue Is Cable-Related or Device-Related
steps.instructions: If the error clears with a known-good cable, replace the accessory. If multiple known-good cables fail, remove the defibrillator from service for bench evaluation or repair.

CCR.Complaint: ZOLL R Series defibrillator reported CHECK ECG CABLE error. Staff stated ECG waveform was not displaying reliably through the ECG cable.
CCR.Cause: ECG trunk cable failed cable recognition testing. CHECK ECG CABLE error cleared when a known-good compatible ECG cable was installed.
CCR.Resolution: Replaced defective ECG cable. Verified ECG monitoring using ECG simulator. Confirmed stable waveform, heart rate display, and no CHECK ECG CABLE error. Device returned to service.

title: ZOLL R Series Defibrillator - Error: CHECK RECORDER
description: Troubleshooting guide for ZOLL R Series CHECK RECORDER errors caused by recorder paper problems, paper jams, door or latch issues, loading errors, or recorder hardware faults.

steps.title: Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Do not troubleshoot the recorder while the defibrillator is needed for active patient care. Remove the unit from patient use if documentation, event printing, or readiness confidence is affected, and use another defibrillator if patient care is active or expected.

steps.title: Verify the Reported Error and Behavior
steps.instructions: Confirm that the exact displayed message is CHECK RECORDER. Observe whether the error appears at startup, during printing, after pressing the recorder button, or intermittently. Note whether the recorder fails to print, feeds poorly, makes noise without moving paper, stops mid-print, or shows no response.

steps.title: Check the Recorder Paper Supply
steps.instructions: Open the recorder compartment and verify that paper is installed. Check for an empty, loose, crushed, wet, contaminated, or backward paper roll. Install a known-good ZOLL-compatible recorder paper roll if needed and attempt a test print.

steps.title: Check for Paper Jam or Obstruction
steps.instructions: Inspect the recorder paper path for torn paper, folded paper, adhesive residue, labels, debris, or paper fragments. Clear any obstruction, confirm smooth paper feed, close the door, and run a test print.

steps.title: Confirm the Recorder Door Is Fully Closed
steps.instructions: Open and close the recorder door firmly. Confirm the latch engages and inspect for cracks, broken hinges, loose latch points, or anything preventing full closure. Perform a test strip if reseating the door clears the error.

steps.title: Verify Correct Paper Orientation
steps.instructions: Confirm that the thermal paper is loaded with the print side facing the correct direction for the recorder head. Feed the paper through the recorder path properly and run a test print.

steps.title: Check for Physical Damage or Contamination
steps.instructions: Inspect the recorder door, latch, paper roller, and visible paper path for damage, fluid contamination, debris, burnt smell, grinding, clicking, or other abnormal signs. Remove the unit from service if damage or contamination is found.

steps.title: Power Cycle and Recheck
steps.instructions: After external checks are complete, turn the unit off, wait briefly, and power it back on. Confirm whether CHECK RECORDER returns. If the message clears, complete a successful test print before returning the device to service.

steps.title: Isolate User-Correctable vs Device-Related Failure
steps.instructions: If paper supply, paper loading, paper path, recorder door, latch condition, and power cycle checks do not resolve the problem, treat the condition as a likely recorder assembly, sensor, latch detection, motor, thermal print mechanism, or internal control issue.

CCR.Complaint: ZOLL R Series displayed CHECK RECORDER error and staff reported the recorder would not print a rhythm strip during use.
CCR.Cause: Recorder paper path inspected. Paper roll was empty and recorder could not feed paper. No physical damage was found.
CCR.Resolution: Installed new compatible recorder paper roll, verified correct orientation, closed recorder door, power cycled unit, and completed successful test print. Device returned to service.

title: ZOLL R Series Defibrillator - Error: RECORDER FAULT 142
description: Troubleshooting guide for ZOLL R Series RECORDER FAULT 142, a strip chart recorder system error that may affect printing, paper feed, event strips, code summary output, or recorder communication.

steps.title: Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Remove the ZOLL R Series from patient use if the recorder fault affects documentation printing, event strip output, or confidence in device reliability. Use another defibrillator if monitoring, pacing, cardioversion, or defibrillation may be needed.

steps.title: Verify the Reported Error and Behavior
steps.instructions: Confirm the exact displayed message is RECORDER FAULT 142. Determine whether it appears at startup, during self-test, when pressing the recorder button, during rhythm strip printing, during code summary printing, or intermittently during use.

steps.title: Check Recorder Paper First
steps.instructions: Confirm paper is installed, loaded in the correct direction, and not jammed, torn, folded, wet, or obstructed. Reload the paper and close the recorder door firmly before retesting.

steps.title: Inspect the Recorder Door and Latch
steps.instructions: Open and close the recorder door. Check for cracked plastic, loose hinges, broken latch tabs, debris, or anything preventing the door from sitting flush with the recorder assembly.

steps.title: Check for Paper Path Obstruction
steps.instructions: Remove the paper roll and inspect the strip chart path for paper fragments, adhesive residue, dirt, or foreign material. Do not force tools into the recorder mechanism. Reload paper and retest printing.

steps.title: Check Power and Startup Behavior
steps.instructions: Power the unit off, connect to known good AC power, confirm normal AC indicator behavior, power the unit on, allow startup to complete, and retest the recorder.

steps.title: Test Recorder Function
steps.instructions: With the device out of patient use, press the recorder or print button. Note whether the recorder starts printing, feeds paper, prints blank paper, prints distorted output, makes abnormal motor noise, or fails immediately with RECORDER FAULT 142.

steps.title: Inspect External Physical Condition
steps.instructions: Inspect the recorder area and housing for cracks, fluid residue, missing parts, bent components, evidence of drops, burning smell, heat damage, or contamination. Remove the device from service if damage or fluid intrusion is found.

steps.title: Narrow the Fault Area
steps.instructions: Rule out paper loading, paper jam, recorder door, paper path obstruction, and power/startup issues before suspecting the recorder assembly, motor, printhead, sensor, internal interconnect, or digital board control path.

steps.title: Stop When Resolved
steps.instructions: If the recorder prints normally and RECORDER FAULT 142 no longer appears, reload paper properly, run an operational check, confirm defibrillator, monitor, and recorder functions pass, document the correction, and return the device to service.

CCR.Complaint: ZOLL R Series displayed RECORDER FAULT 142 and staff reported the strip chart recorder would not print during recorder test.
CCR.Cause: Recorder paper was loaded correctly and no paper jam, door issue, power issue, or external obstruction was found. Fault remained present during recorder test, indicating likely internal recorder assembly, interconnect, or digital board path failure.
CCR.Resolution: Removed device from service, labeled Out of Service, and sent for bench evaluation/repair. Recorder fault remained present after external checks.

title: ZOLL R Series Defibrillator - Error: BATTERY COMMS ERROR
description: Troubleshooting guide for BATTERY COMMS ERROR on the ZOLL R Series defibrillator when the device cannot properly communicate with the installed battery, affecting battery recognition, status reporting, and portable-use reliability.

steps.title: Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Remove the defibrillator from patient use if BATTERY COMMS ERROR is active. Replace it with a known-good defibrillator if emergency defibrillation, pacing, cardioversion, or monitoring may be needed. Do not rely on battery operation while this error is present.

steps.title: Verify the Reported Error and Behavior
steps.instructions: Power the ZOLL R Series on and confirm the displayed message is BATTERY COMMS ERROR. Note whether it appears at startup, after battery insertion, while running on battery power, or intermittently. Observe whether the unit recognizes the battery and whether it operates normally on AC power.

steps.title: Check AC Power First
steps.instructions: Connect the unit to a known-good AC power source. Confirm the AC indicator is present, allow the unit to remain connected briefly, and power cycle the device while on AC power.

steps.title: Inspect the Battery
steps.instructions: Remove the installed battery and inspect it for cracked housing, swelling, contamination, leakage, damaged contacts, or impact damage. Confirm the battery is compatible with the ZOLL R Series. Do not use a physically damaged battery.

steps.title: Reseat the Battery
steps.instructions: Remove the battery completely, inspect the battery compartment for debris or obstruction, reinstall the battery fully, confirm it latches securely, and power the device back on.

steps.title: Try a Known-Good Battery
steps.instructions: Install a known-good compatible ZOLL R Series battery and observe whether BATTERY COMMS ERROR returns. If the error clears, the original battery is likely defective. If the error remains, the issue likely stays with the defibrillator.

steps.title: Test the Suspect Battery in Another Compatible Unit
steps.instructions: If available, install the suspect battery into another known-good compatible R Series unit. If the same error appears, remove the battery from service. If the second unit reads the battery normally, suspect the original defibrillator.

steps.title: Inspect the Battery Compartment and Contacts
steps.instructions: Inspect the battery bay for bent contacts, recessed pins, contamination, corrosion, loose parts, liquid intrusion, or uneven battery seating. Do not scrape, bend, force, or modify internal contacts.

steps.title: Confirm Charging and Battery Recognition Behavior
steps.instructions: With AC connected and a known-good battery installed, check for expected charging and battery status behavior. Run the facility-approved operational checkout if the error clears.

steps.title: Determine Whether the Issue Is Battery-Related or Device-Related
steps.instructions: Use battery swap results to determine whether the error follows one battery or remains with the defibrillator. Remove the unit from service if the error remains with multiple known-good batteries or if the battery bay appears damaged.

CCR.Complaint: ZOLL R Series defibrillator displayed BATTERY COMMS ERROR and staff reported the unit would not properly recognize or communicate with the installed battery.
CCR.Cause: Battery communication fault confirmed. AC power was verified, the battery was reseated, the battery bay was inspected, and a known-good compatible battery was tested. Error remained with the defibrillator, indicating likely device-side battery communication failure.
CCR.Resolution: Removed defibrillator from service and labeled Out of Service. Documented battery IDs tested and sent unit for bench evaluation or repair for suspected battery interconnect or device-side communication issue.

title: ZOLL R Series Defibrillator - Error: BATT HIGH VOLTAGE
description: Troubleshooting guide for a ZOLL R Series BATT HIGH VOLTAGE error indicating charger voltage is too high, which may affect battery charging, AC operation, and defibrillator readiness.

steps.title: Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Remove the defibrillator from patient use if the BATT HIGH VOLTAGE error is active or recurring. Transfer defibrillation, pacing, and monitoring needs to another ready defibrillator. Do not rely on a defibrillator with an unresolved battery or charging system error.

steps.title: Verify the Reported Error and Behavior
steps.instructions: Confirm that the displayed message reads BATT HIGH VOLTAGE. Determine whether the error appears on startup, while connected to AC power, while running on battery, during charging, or intermittently after being stored on charge.

steps.title: Remove the Device From AC Power and Check Battery Operation
steps.instructions: Unplug the R Series from AC power and power the unit on using battery power only. Observe whether the error remains, clears, or changes to help separate AC charger behavior from battery-related behavior.

steps.title: Inspect the Battery Pack
steps.instructions: Remove the battery and inspect it for cracked housing, swelling, leaking, burn marks, damaged contacts, contamination, or loose fit. Remove any damaged, hot, swollen, or leaking battery from service.

steps.title: Reseat the Battery
steps.instructions: Power the defibrillator off, remove the battery, inspect the contacts and battery compartment, reinstall the battery firmly, and power the unit back on. Confirm whether the error returns.

steps.title: Test With a Known-Good Battery
steps.instructions: Install a known-good compatible ZOLL R Series battery. Power the unit on, connect AC power, and observe charging behavior. If the error clears, the original battery is suspect. If it remains, the device charger or AC charging circuit is suspect.

steps.title: Check AC Power Source and Power Cord
steps.instructions: Verify the device is connected to a proper hospital-grade outlet. Inspect the AC cord for damage, loose plug, bent prongs, damaged strain relief, or intermittent connection. Try a known-good cord and verified outlet if available.

steps.title: Observe Charging Behavior on AC Power
steps.instructions: With a known-good battery installed, connect AC power and watch for immediate return of the error, abnormal battery indication, failure to charge, service indicators, heat, odor, or unusual sounds.

steps.title: Run Required Readiness or Operational Checks
steps.instructions: If the error clears, perform the facility-required defibrillator readiness check. Verify normal power-on behavior, no active error message, normal battery and AC indicators, passing readiness status, and required ECG, printer, and alarm functions.

CCR.Complaint: ZOLL R Series defibrillator reported with BATT HIGH VOLTAGE error. Staff stated unit displayed a battery/charger fault while connected to AC power and may not be maintaining normal battery charge readiness.
CCR.Cause: Confirmed BATT HIGH VOLTAGE error. Battery and charging system issue observed. External checks performed including battery reseat, battery inspection, AC cord and outlet check, and known-good battery test. Error followed original battery or remained with known-good battery.
CCR.Resolution: Removed unit from patient use during troubleshooting. Tested with known-good battery and verified AC power source. Replaced failed battery and completed readiness check, or labeled unit Out of Service and sent for bench evaluation for suspected AC charger fault.

title: ZOLL X Series Defibrillator - NIBP Cuff Inflation or Blood Pressure Measurement Failure
description: Troubleshooting failed cuff inflation, repeated NIBP errors, incomplete measurements, or questionable readings caused by cuffs, tubing, connections, settings, or patient conditions.

steps.title: 1. Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Do not perform extended NIBP troubleshooting while the X Series is the only device monitoring an unstable patient. If blood-pressure monitoring is clinically necessary: Notify the clinical provider that the NIBP measurement is unavailable or unreliable. Obtain blood pressure using another verified monitor or an approved manual method. Continue ECG, SpO₂, and other appropriate monitoring. Replace the X Series if reliable blood-pressure monitoring cannot be maintained. Expected outcome: Patient care does not depend on an unresolved NIBP measurement problem. Continue troubleshooting only when it is safe to remove the device or NIBP function from active patient use.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Failure
steps.instructions: Attempt one NIBP measurement and observe whether: The cuff does not inflate. The cuff begins inflating but immediately deflates. Inflation continues longer than expected. The measurement ends without displaying a result. The displayed value appears inconsistent with the patient’s condition. A specific NIBP message or error appears. Record the complete displayed message and the stage at which the measurement fails. Expected outcome: The failure is narrowed to inflation, pressure retention, signal acquisition, or result accuracy.

steps.title: 3. Verify the NIBP Function Is Available and Selected
steps.instructions: Confirm that: The device configuration includes NIBP capability. The NIBP parameter is displayed. The correct patient type is selected. A manual measurement is initiated from the appropriate NIBP control. Automatic interval mode is configured correctly when that mode is being used. The X Series supports manual and configurable interval-based NIBP measurements. Expected outcome: The monitor accepts the measurement command and begins the NIBP cycle. If the measurement now operates normally, verify performance and stop.

steps.title: 4. Inspect the Cuff
steps.instructions: Remove the cuff from the patient and inspect it for: Tears, holes, or separated seams. Damaged hook-and-loop material. A twisted or folded bladder. Contamination or fluid intrusion. A damaged hose fitting. Incorrect cuff type or size. Use an appropriately sized, compatible cuff for the selected patient population. Expected outcome: The cuff is intact, correctly sized, and capable of holding pressure. If damage is found, replace the cuff and repeat the measurement. If the issue is resolved, stop.

steps.title: 5. Check Cuff Placement and Patient Conditions
steps.instructions: Verify that the cuff: Is applied to a suitable limb. Is positioned over bare skin when possible. Fits snugly without being excessively tight. Has its artery-position marker aligned correctly. Is not placed over thick clothing, tubing, or another device. Is not affected by patient movement, shivering, or transport vibration. Also consider whether weak perfusion, severe arrhythmia, rapid pressure changes, or limb movement may prevent a reliable oscillometric reading. Expected outcome: The cuff is positioned correctly and measurement conditions are suitable. If proper placement resolves the problem, confirm a repeatable reading and stop.

steps.title: 6. Inspect the NIBP Hose
steps.instructions: Examine the entire hose for: Kinks or compression. Cuts, cracks, or punctures. Loose fittings. Stretched or damaged connectors. Internal blockage. Contamination or moisture. Straighten the hose and ensure it is not trapped beneath the patient, mattress, stretcher rail, or equipment. Expected outcome: The hose provides an unrestricted, sealed pneumatic path. If the hose is damaged, replace it with a compatible known-good hose and retest.

steps.title: 7. Reseat the Pneumatic Connections
steps.instructions: Disconnect and reconnect: The cuff-to-hose connection. The hose-to-monitor NIBP connection. Ensure each fitting is fully seated and does not loosen when gently moved. Do not force a connector or use an incompatible adapter. Expected outcome: The cuff and hose remain securely connected throughout inflation. If reseating the connections restores normal operation, complete several measurements and stop.

steps.title: 8. Test With Known-Good Accessories
steps.instructions: Install: A known-good compatible NIBP cuff. A known-good compatible NIBP hose. Test the cuff around an appropriate test mandrel, simulator sleeve, or suitable non-patient test setup. Change one accessory at a time when practical so the failed component can be identified. Expected outcome: The monitor completes inflation and produces a measurement with known-good accessories. If replacing the cuff or hose resolves the failure, remove the defective accessory from service and document it.

steps.title: 9. Check for an External Air Leak
steps.instructions: During a test measurement, listen and feel for escaping air around: The cuff bladder. Cuff fittings. Hose connections. The hose body. The monitor connection. A cuff that inflates slowly, fails to reach pressure, or immediately deflates may have an external pneumatic leak. Expected outcome: The cuff inflates without audible leakage and maintains pressure during the measurement cycle. If an external leak is identified, replace the affected accessory and stop.

steps.title: 10. Restart the Monitor
steps.instructions: When clinically safe: Turn the X Series off. Disconnect it from patient use. Wait briefly. Restart the device. Allow startup checks to complete. Repeat the NIBP test with known-good accessories. Expected outcome: The NIBP control initializes and performs a normal measurement cycle. If restarting resolves the issue, perform repeated measurements before returning the device to service.

steps.title: 11. Compare the Reading With a Reference
steps.instructions: If the unit completes measurements but the values appear inaccurate: Use an approved NIBP simulator when available. Select appropriate adult, pediatric, or neonatal test parameters. Compare displayed systolic, diastolic, and mean values with the simulator’s expected values. Repeat the test at more than one pressure level. Confirm that the cuff and hose do not leak. Do not judge accuracy using a single comparison against another automatic monitor on a moving or clinically unstable patient. Expected outcome: Measurements remain within the facility’s acceptance criteria and the manufacturer’s applicable specifications. If readings remain inconsistent or outside tolerance with a simulator and known-good accessories, discontinue testing and escalate.

steps.title: 12. Check for Repeated Abnormal Pump or Valve Behavior
steps.instructions: Remove the device from service if you observe: No pump sound or airflow during an initiated measurement. Continuous pumping without normal pressure control. Immediate venting with known-good accessories. Abnormally loud, weak, or irregular pump operation. Failure to release cuff pressure. Repeated internal NIBP errors. Excessive heat, odor, or unusual sounds. Do not open the device or perform internal pneumatic repair unless authorized, trained, and working under the applicable ZOLL service procedure. Expected outcome: Internal pump, valve, pressure-sensor, or pneumatic-control concerns are recognized and escalated appropriately.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that the ZOLL X Series NIBP cuff would begin inflating but terminate without displaying a blood-pressure result.
CCR.Cause: Inspection found a pneumatic leak at the cuff hose connector, and the monitor completed normal measurements when tested with a known-good cuff and hose.
CCR.Resolution: Replaced the damaged NIBP hose, completed repeated NIBP simulator tests at multiple pressure settings, verified acceptable operation, and returned the device to service.

title: ZOLL X Series Defibrillator - SpO2 Sensor Not Detected or Intermittent Saturation Reading
description: Troubleshooting missing or unstable SpO2 readings caused by sensor application, motion, contamination, damaged accessories, poor connections, or configuration issues.

steps.title: Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Do not perform extended SpO2 troubleshooting while the X Series is the only device monitoring a patient who requires continuous oxygen-saturation assessment. If SpO2 monitoring becomes unavailable during patient care: Notify the clinical provider. Assess the patient using clinical observations and other available monitoring. Apply an independent pulse oximeter when continuous SpO2 monitoring is required. Replace the monitor or SpO2 accessory if reliable readings cannot be restored promptly. Expected outcome: Patient care does not depend on an unreliable or unavailable SpO2 measurement. Continue troubleshooting only when it is safe to disconnect or exchange the SpO2 accessories.

steps.title: Confirm the Exact Failure Condition
steps.instructions: Determine whether: No SpO2 value appears. The device reports that the sensor is not detected. A reading appears and disappears intermittently. The waveform is weak, erratic, or absent. The displayed pulse rate does not correspond with the patient’s actual pulse. The problem occurs with one sensor or with every sensor tested. Record any displayed message and whether an SpO2 waveform or signal-quality indication is present. Expected outcome: The problem is clearly categorized as a detection, signal-quality, accessory, or monitor-related issue.

steps.title: Verify That SpO2 Monitoring Is Installed and Enabled
steps.instructions: Confirm that the X Series is configured with the SpO2 monitoring option and that the SpO2 parameter is enabled in the current display configuration. The X Series supports SpO2 as an optional physiologic monitoring parameter. Expected outcome: The SpO2 parameter area appears and is available for monitoring. If SpO2 is not installed or enabled, correct the approved configuration or escalate according to facility policy.

steps.title: Inspect the Sensor Application
steps.instructions: Check that: The sensor is positioned on the correct anatomical site. The emitter and detector are aligned across the tissue. The sensor is not excessively loose or tight. The selected sensor is appropriate for the patient and application site. The sensor is not placed over nail polish, artificial nails, heavy contamination, or damaged tissue. The site has adequate perfusion. Reposition the sensor or test another appropriate site when clinically safe. Expected outcome: A stable plethysmographic waveform and SpO2 value appear. If the reading becomes stable, the issue was related to sensor placement or site conditions. Stop troubleshooting.

steps.title: Eliminate Motion and Environmental Interference
steps.instructions: Keep the test site still and check for: Patient movement or tremor. Vibration during transport. Bright surgical or examination lighting directed at the sensor. Repeated blood-pressure cuff inflation on the same limb. Compression, venous congestion, or reduced circulation at the sensor site. Electrosurgical or other electrical interference. Shield or reposition the sensor and retest under controlled conditions. Expected outcome: The waveform becomes stable and the saturation value remains continuously displayed. If the issue resolves, document the source of interference and stop troubleshooting.

steps.title: Inspect the SpO2 Sensor
steps.instructions: Disconnect the sensor and visually inspect it for: Cracked or damaged housing. Torn insulation. Frayed or sharply kinked cable sections. Contamination on the optical surfaces. Fluid intrusion. Bent, recessed, corroded, or contaminated connector contacts. Damage near strain-relief points. Clean the accessory only with an approved method and allow it to dry completely before testing. Do not use a sensor with exposed conductors, fluid intrusion, damaged contacts, or compromised insulation. Expected outcome: The sensor is clean, dry, intact, and suitable for testing. Replace visibly damaged accessories before proceeding.

steps.title: Inspect and Reseat All SpO2 Connections
steps.instructions: Disconnect and reconnect: The patient sensor from the extension or interface cable. The interface cable from the X Series SpO2 input. Align connectors correctly and insert them fully without forcing them. Check for looseness or intermittent contact while gently supporting the connector—not by sharply flexing the cable. Expected outcome: The monitor consistently recognizes the sensor without the reading dropping out. If reseating restores reliable operation, confirm stability and stop troubleshooting.

steps.title: Test With a Known-Good Compatible Sensor
steps.instructions: Replace the original sensor with a known-good, approved sensor of the correct type. Do not assume that a sensor is functional because its cable and housing appear undamaged. Internal conductor or optical-component failures may be intermittent. Expected outcome: If the known-good sensor works, remove the original sensor from use. If both sensors fail, continue to the interface-cable check.

steps.title: Test the SpO2 Interface or Extension Cable
steps.instructions: When a separate interface or extension cable is used, replace it with a known-good compatible cable. Pay particular attention to failures that occur when the cable is moved near: The monitor connector. The sensor connector. Strain-relief sections. Previously kinked or tightly wrapped areas. Expected outcome: If the replacement cable restores stable readings, remove the original cable from service. If the problem remains, continue troubleshooting.

steps.title: Confirm Accessory Compatibility
steps.instructions: Verify that the sensor and interface cable are: Approved for the installed SpO2 technology. Correctly matched to each other. Intended for the patient population and monitoring application. Within any applicable reuse or service-life limitations. Do not mix visually similar sensors, adapters, or cables from incompatible monitoring platforms. Expected outcome: All connected components form a compatible SpO2 accessory system. If replacing an incompatible component resolves the issue, stop troubleshooting.

steps.title: Inspect the Monitor’s SpO2 Input Connector
steps.instructions: With the device removed from patient use, inspect the external SpO2 port for: Bent or damaged contacts. Foreign material. Fluid residue. Cracks or looseness. A connector that does not retain the cable securely. Do not insert tools into the connector or attempt contact repair without authorized service procedures. Expected outcome: The connector is clean, secure, and free of visible damage. Visible port damage requires removal from service and repair evaluation.

steps.title: Restart and Retest the X Series
steps.instructions: When clinically safe: Disconnect the SpO2 accessories. Power the X Series off normally. Wait for shutdown to complete. Reconnect a known-good SpO2 cable and sensor. Power the device on. Verify sensor detection and monitor the reading for several minutes. Expected outcome: The monitor initializes the SpO2 channel and maintains a stable waveform and saturation value. If restarting resolves the problem, complete an operational check before returning the device to service.

steps.title: Compare the SpO2 Pulse Rate With an Independent Source
steps.instructions: Compare the pulse rate derived from SpO2 with: The patient’s palpated pulse. ECG heart rate. A verified pulse-oximeter simulator. Another approved monitor. A saturation number without a credible waveform or matching pulse rate should not be accepted as a valid reading. Expected outcome: SpO2 pulse rate, waveform, and saturation are internally consistent and agree reasonably with the reference.

steps.title: Perform an Approved Functional Test
steps.instructions: Use a compatible pulse-oximeter simulator or the facility’s approved functional-testing method. Test: Sensor detection. Stable SpO2 display. Pulse-rate response. Waveform stability. Alarm operation, when included in the facility procedure. Cable stability during gentle movement. Follow the simulator manufacturer’s instructions and the facility’s approved acceptance criteria. Do not interpret a simulator test as a complete calibration unless the applicable service documentation defines it that way. Expected outcome: SpO2 monitoring operates consistently across the approved test conditions. If the device fails with known-good accessories and a verified simulator, discontinue troubleshooting and escalate.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that the ZOLL X Series intermittently displayed no SpO2 value and repeatedly lost the pulse-oximetry waveform.
CCR.Cause: Inspection and substitution testing identified an intermittent open connection in the reusable SpO2 interface cable near the sensor connector.
CCR.Resolution: Removed the damaged cable from service, installed a known-good compatible cable, and verified stable SpO2, pulse rate, waveform, and alarm operation using an approved simulator.

helpfulDetails: Condition of connectors and strain reliefs.
Whether movement caused the reading to drop.
Evidence of fluid intrusion or contamination.

title: ZOLL X Series Defibrillator - EtCO₂ FilterLine / Sampling Failure or No Capnogram
description: Troubleshooting absent EtCO₂ values, missing capnograms, sampling alarms, or unreliable readings caused by FilterLine, airway-adapter, connection, moisture, or configuration problems.

steps.title: 1. Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Do not perform extended capnography troubleshooting while the ZOLL X Series is the only device monitoring ventilation on an active patient. If EtCO₂ monitoring becomes unavailable during patient care: Notify the responsible clinical provider immediately. Assess ventilation using chest movement, respiratory rate, oxygen saturation, airway pressure, and another approved monitoring method. Replace the monitor or use an independent capnography device when continuous EtCO₂ monitoring is clinically required. Do not delay ventilation or airway interventions while troubleshooting the monitor. Expected outcome: Patient ventilation remains appropriately monitored without relying on questionable EtCO₂ readings. Continue troubleshooting only after the device can be safely evaluated.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Failure Condition
steps.instructions: Record the complete message displayed by the X Series and determine whether: No EtCO₂ numerical value is displayed. The numerical value appears without a capnogram. The capnogram is intermittent or unusually flat. A sampling-line, occlusion, or initialization message is present. The problem occurs with one FilterLine or every FilterLine tested. Confirm that the reported problem is EtCO₂-specific and that the monitor otherwise powers on and operates normally. Expected outcome: The failure is clearly identified before accessories are replaced.

steps.title: 3. Verify That EtCO₂ Monitoring Is Enabled
steps.instructions: Confirm that: The EtCO₂ parameter is enabled in the monitoring display. The capnogram waveform is selected for an available waveform channel. Appropriate patient type and alarm settings are selected. The displayed scale or waveform position is not making a small waveform difficult to see. The X Series supports optional capnography configurations, so parameter availability depends on the device’s installed options and configuration. Expected outcome: The EtCO₂ value and waveform areas are present and ready to display sampled CO₂. If the capnogram appears after correcting the display configuration, verify operation and stop.

steps.title: 4. Inspect the FilterLine Connection
steps.instructions: Disconnect and reconnect the FilterLine at the X Series CO₂ sampling port. Check that: The connector is fully seated. The connector is not loose, cracked, bent, or contaminated. The tubing is not pulling sideways against the port. No packaging cap or protective cover remains installed. The sampling line is compatible with the monitor and intended clinical application. Allow the monitor sufficient time to recognize the line and initialize sampling. Expected outcome: The monitor recognizes the connected FilterLine without a persistent sampling message. If reconnecting the line restores stable EtCO₂ monitoring, verify the capnogram and stop.

steps.title: 5. Inspect the Entire Sampling Line
steps.instructions: Trace the FilterLine from the monitor to the patient connection. Look for: Kinked or sharply bent tubing. Tubing trapped under equipment or stretcher rails. Stretched, crushed, cut, or disconnected tubing. Loose connections at the airway adapter, cannula, or mask. Condensation, secretions, blood, medication residue, or visible contamination. An incorrect or damaged airway adapter. Do not insert wires, tools, compressed air, or cleaning solution into the FilterLine or monitor sampling port. Expected outcome: The sampling path is open, dry, intact, and properly connected. If correcting a kink or loose connection restores the waveform, verify stable operation and stop.

steps.title: 6. Replace the FilterLine and Patient Interface
steps.instructions: Install a new, approved FilterLine and the correct patient interface for the intended application. Replace the complete disposable sampling assembly when: Moisture or contamination is visible. The line appears restricted. The connector is damaged. The line has already been used on a patient. The problem follows the original FilterLine. Do not attempt to clean or repair a disposable sampling line. Expected outcome: A known-good FilterLine is recognized and produces a stable EtCO₂ value and capnogram. If a replacement FilterLine resolves the issue, remove the defective disposable from use and stop.

steps.title: 7. Confirm the Patient Interface and Sampling Location
steps.instructions: For intubated monitoring, verify that: The airway adapter is installed in the correct orientation. Connections are tight. The adapter is not filled with condensation or secretions. The sampling location is not excessively distant from the airway. For non-intubated monitoring, verify that: The nasal or oral-nasal cannula is positioned correctly. The patient is breathing through the intended sampling pathway. Supplemental oxygen tubing is connected to the correct port when applicable. The cannula is not displaced or obstructed. A flat or weak capnogram may result from poor sample collection even when the monitor and FilterLine are functioning. Expected outcome: Exhaled gas reaches the sampling line consistently. If repositioning or replacing the patient interface produces a normal capnogram, verify operation and stop.

steps.title: 8. Allow the Sampling System to Stabilize
steps.instructions: After installing a new FilterLine: Allow the X Series to complete initialization. Observe whether the displayed message clears. Confirm that the sampling pump can be heard faintly when appropriate. Watch for a consistent waveform over several respiratory cycles. Do not condemn the monitor immediately if a temporary initialization message appears after connecting a new line. Expected outcome: The monitor completes startup and begins displaying sampled CO₂.

steps.title: 9. Test With a Known-Good External Setup
steps.instructions: Remove the device from patient use and connect: A new approved FilterLine. A known-good airway adapter or cannula. An appropriate capnography simulator or controlled test source capable of producing repeatable CO₂ waveforms. Do not rely only on briefly breathing into the sampling assembly as the final performance test. Verify: EtCO₂ numerical response. Respiratory-rate response. Capnogram appearance. EtCO₂ alarm operation. Stability without sampling or occlusion messages. Expected outcome: The X Series displays a repeatable EtCO₂ value and recognizable capnogram. If the device functions with the controlled test setup, the original FilterLine, patient interface, or clinical setup was the likely cause.

steps.title: 10. Compare With Another Known-Good FilterLine
steps.instructions: When available, test the suspected FilterLine on another compatible, verified monitor or test the X Series using a FilterLine known to work on another device. Do not transfer a used patient accessory between patients. Interpret the results: If the failure follows the FilterLine, replace the disposable accessory. If multiple known-good FilterLines fail only on the same X Series, suspect a monitor sampling-port, pump, pneumatic, configuration, or internal capnography-module problem. Expected outcome: The problem is isolated to either the accessory or the monitor.

steps.title: 11. Inspect the Monitor Sampling Port Externally
steps.instructions: With the device removed from service, inspect the EtCO₂ sampling port for: Cracks or physical damage. A loose or recessed connector. Visible liquid or debris. Signs that a connector was forced into the port. Evidence of impact damage near the port. Do not open the device or insert tools into the sampling port. Internal pneumatic inspection and repair should follow authorized ZOLL service procedures. Expected outcome: The external port is intact, clean, and able to retain the FilterLine connector securely.

steps.title: 12. Perform a Final Functional Check
steps.instructions: After correcting the problem: Restart the monitor when clinically appropriate. Install a known-good FilterLine. Confirm a stable EtCO₂ value and capnogram. Verify respiratory-rate calculation. Test applicable EtCO₂ alarms. Confirm that no sampling, occlusion, or module messages remain. Return the monitor to service only after all required operational checks pass. Expected outcome: Capnography operates consistently without intermittent loss or accessory-related alarms.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that the ZOLL X Series displayed no EtCO₂ value or capnogram after connecting the patient FilterLine.
CCR.Cause: The installed FilterLine was visibly kinked near the airway adapter and remained restricted when tested off the patient.
CCR.Resolution: Removed the damaged FilterLine, installed a new approved sampling line, and verified stable EtCO₂, respiratory rate, capnogram, and alarm operation using a controlled test setup.

title: ZOLL X Series Defibrillator - External Pacing Will Not Capture or Pacer Output Issue
description: Troubleshooting absent electrical or mechanical capture, pacing-electrode connection problems, poor pad contact, incorrect settings, or suspected pacer-output failure.

steps.title: 1. Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Do not perform extended pacing troubleshooting while the X Series is the only device supporting an unstable patient. If external pacing is unsuccessful during clinical use: Notify the responsible clinical provider immediately. Continue ECG, pulse, blood-pressure, oxygen-saturation, and patient assessment. Prepare another verified defibrillator with external pacing capability. Follow the facility’s emergency bradycardia and equipment-failure procedures. Transfer pacing support to another device when capture cannot be established promptly. Expected outcome: Patient care does not remain dependent on equipment with uncertain pacing performance. Continue Clinical Engineering troubleshooting only after the device is safely removed from patient use.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Reported Failure
steps.instructions: Determine whether the complaint involves: Pacer mode will not activate. The pacing rate or current cannot be adjusted. No pacing markers appear on the ECG display. Pacing markers appear, but no ECG capture occurs. ECG capture appears without a corresponding pulse. A pads-off, poor-contact, or electrode-related message appears. The pacing current stops unexpectedly. Record the selected pacing rate, selected current in milliamperes, ECG lead, electrode type, displayed messages, and whether the problem occurred continuously or intermittently. Expected outcome: The complaint is separated into an operating, connection, electrical-capture, mechanical-capture, or output-performance problem.

steps.title: 3. Verify the Device Is in Pacer Mode
steps.instructions: Confirm that the X Series is operating in manual mode and that pacing has been selected according to the facility-approved operating process. Verify that: The pacer controls are displayed. A pacing rate is selected. Pacing current is above zero. The pacer is actively running rather than paused. Expected outcome: Pacing markers and the selected pacing settings appear on the display. If the controls now function normally, complete an operational check and stop troubleshooting.

steps.title: 4. Check the Therapy Cable Connection
steps.instructions: Inspect the multifunction therapy cable and confirm that it is fully seated in the X Series therapy connector. Check for: A partially inserted connector. A loose locking connection. Bent, recessed, contaminated, or damaged contacts. Cracked connector housings. Cable cuts, crushed sections, severe kinks, or exposed conductors. Disconnect and reconnect the cable only when the device is not connected to a patient. Expected outcome: The therapy cable connects securely without movement, intermittent messages, or visible damage. If reseating the connection restores stable pacing operation, verify the device with an approved analyzer and stop.

steps.title: 5. Verify the Correct Pacing Electrodes Are Installed
steps.instructions: Confirm that compatible ZOLL multifunction electrodes approved for pacing are being used and that they are within their expiration date. Inspect the package and electrodes for: Open or damaged packaging. Dried or uneven conductive gel. Folded, contaminated, or damaged adhesive surfaces. Incorrect adult or pediatric electrode selection. Damage to the electrode lead or connector. ZOLL multifunction electrodes provide the current path used for external pacing, so defective, expired, or poorly connected electrodes can prevent effective current delivery. Expected outcome: A new, compatible, undamaged electrode set is connected securely. If replacing the electrodes resolves the issue, remove the defective set from use and document the lot and expiration information when available.

steps.title: 6. Check Electrode Placement and Contact
steps.instructions: When evaluating a clinical report, confirm that the patient’s skin was exposed, dry, and prepared according to facility protocol. Verify that: Electrodes were positioned as directed on their packaging. The entire conductive surface adhered to the skin. Excessive hair, moisture, oils, medication patches, clothing, or trapped air did not interfere with contact. The pads were not overlapping or touching. The placement created an appropriate current path through the heart. Poor adhesion, moisture, hair, or improper positioning can increase transthoracic resistance and reduce current delivery. Expected outcome: Electrodes have complete skin contact and the pads-off or poor-contact indication clears. Clinical Engineering should not reproduce pacing on a person. Use an approved defibrillator/pacer analyzer for bench verification.

steps.title: 7. Confirm the ECG Signal Is Suitable for Pacing
steps.instructions: Inspect the displayed ECG waveform. Verify that: The ECG waveform is visible and reasonably free of artifact. The selected ECG lead produces clear QRS complexes. Lead wires and electrodes are securely connected when separate ECG leads are used. Pacing spikes are not being confused with motion artifact or unrelated ECG noise. The display gain allows the technician or clinician to distinguish intrinsic complexes from paced complexes. Expected outcome: The underlying rhythm and pacing markers can be evaluated reliably. If changing a loose ECG cable, electrode, or lead selection restores a stable display, repeat the functional test and stop.

steps.title: 8. Distinguish Electrical Capture From Mechanical Capture
steps.instructions: Electrical capture is suggested when each pacing marker is followed by a consistent widened QRS complex or other expected depolarization pattern. Mechanical capture requires evidence of effective cardiac output, such as: A corresponding palpable pulse. A pulse waveform matching the paced rate. A blood-pressure response. Other approved clinical confirmation. Do not assume capture based only on the presence of pacing markers. Pacing markers indicate a pacing command, not necessarily effective myocardial capture. Expected outcome: The reported problem is correctly identified as failure of electrical capture, failure of mechanical capture, or a display-interpretation issue. Clinical Engineering should document the reported clinical behavior but should not determine patient treatment settings.

steps.title: 9. Review the Reported Pacing Current
steps.instructions: Confirm whether the clinician increased pacing current gradually according to clinical protocol until capture was achieved or the condition was determined to be nonresponsive. A low selected current may produce visible pacing markers without sufficient delivered current to achieve capture. However, the required current varies by patient and is a clinical determination. Expected outcome: The problem is not caused simply by the pacing current remaining at zero or an unintentionally low setting. Do not direct Clinical Engineering staff to establish patient-specific pacing thresholds.

steps.title: 10. Check for Patient-Related High-Impedance Conditions
steps.instructions: Review whether the failed capture occurred under conditions that could increase resistance or make transcutaneous capture difficult, including: Incomplete electrode adhesion. Large body habitus. Excessive chest hair. Very dry or damaged electrodes. Incorrect electrode positioning. Patient movement. Severe physiologic or metabolic conditions reported by the clinical team. Expected outcome: A patient-related capture difficulty is not incorrectly classified as equipment failure. The device must still be bench tested before being returned to service.

steps.title: 11. Test With an Approved Defibrillator/Pacer Analyzer
steps.instructions: Remove the X Series from clinical use and connect it to a calibrated analyzer that supports transcutaneous pacing measurements. Following the analyzer manufacturer’s instructions and the facility’s approved test procedure: Connect the multifunction therapy cable to the analyzer. Select pacer mode. Test multiple pacing rates. Test multiple output-current settings. Confirm that the analyzer detects pacing pulses. Compare measured rate and current with displayed settings. Check for stable output without unexpected interruption. Gently manipulate the external cable near strain-relief points while observing for intermittent output. Expected outcome: The measured pacing rate and output remain stable and within the facility’s approved acceptance criteria. Do not use improvised resistive loads, handheld meters, or direct contact methods to measure pacing output.

steps.title: 12. Substitute Known-Good External Accessories
steps.instructions: When the output is absent or intermittent, repeat the analyzer test using: A known-good compatible therapy cable. A known-good electrode adapter or test connection, when applicable. A second approved analyzer channel or cable when available. Change one component at a time. Expected outcome: The failed component is isolated without assuming an internal defibrillator failure. If pacing operates normally with the known-good cable, remove the original cable from service and replace it.

steps.title: 13. Inspect Power and Battery Status
steps.instructions: Confirm that: A charged, approved battery is installed. The battery is fully seated. No power or battery warning is present. The device remains powered during pacing-output testing. External power, when used, is connected securely. Expected outcome: Pacing is not being interrupted by unstable device power. If the unit restarts, shuts down, or changes operating state during testing, discontinue use and evaluate the power system separately.

steps.title: 14. Perform the Approved Operational or Readiness Check
steps.instructions: Run the facility-approved X Series operational check and review the device for active service indicators or failed readiness results. Verify that defibrillation, monitoring, and pacing-related accessories are correctly connected for the test being performed. Expected outcome: The X Series completes the approved checks without errors. A successful automated check does not override a failed measured pacing-output test or a reproducible intermittent complaint.

steps.title: 15. Compare With the Original Complaint
steps.instructions: After testing, determine whether the failure: Was corrected by replacing electrodes. Was corrected by replacing the therapy cable. Was caused by poor electrode contact or incorrect setup. Could not be reproduced and all analyzer measurements passed. Remains reproducible with known-good accessories. Includes unstable, absent, or inaccurate pacing output. Expected outcome: The final device disposition is supported by repeatable evidence. If the device passes all testing but the original complaint involved intermittent behavior, document the exact accessories tested and consult the reporting department before returning the unit to service.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that the ZOLL X Series displayed pacing markers but external pacing did not produce consistent capture.
CCR.Cause: Bench testing found intermittent pacing output when the multifunction therapy cable was moved near its connector strain relief.
CCR.Resolution: Removed the damaged therapy cable from service, installed a verified replacement, and confirmed stable pacing rate and current at multiple settings with a calibrated defibrillator/pacer analyzer.

helpfulDetails: Electrode type, lot, and expiration date

title: ZOLL X Series Defibrillator - 12-Lead ECG Acquisition or Transmission Failure
description: Troubleshooting failed 12-lead acquisition or transmission caused by electrodes, ECG cables, patient data, device settings, network connectivity, or destination configuration.

steps.title: 1. Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Do not perform extended troubleshooting while the X Series is the only monitor or defibrillator available for an unstable patient. If the failure occurs during active patient care: Notify the clinical team that the 12-lead ECG is unavailable or has not transmitted. Continue rhythm monitoring using an available ECG lead. Obtain a 12-lead using another verified ECG device when urgently required. Keep another defibrillator immediately available if the X Series must be removed from service. Do not delay time-sensitive treatment solely to troubleshoot electronic transmission. Expected outcome: Patient assessment and emergency treatment continue without depending on the failed 12-lead function. Continue troubleshooting only when it is clinically safe.

steps.title: 2. Determine Whether Acquisition or Transmission Failed
steps.instructions: Confirm the exact failure: The 12-lead screen cannot be opened. One or more leads display as disconnected. Waveforms are noisy or unusable. The acquisition will not complete. The ECG acquires but will not print. The ECG saves locally but will not transmit. Transmission begins but reports a connection, server, destination, or communication error. Record the complete displayed message and the time of failure. Expected outcome: The issue is separated into an ECG acquisition problem, a printing problem, or a communication problem.

steps.title: 3. Confirm the 12-Lead Option Is Available
steps.instructions: Verify that the device is configured for 12-lead ECG operation and that the expected 12-lead controls or menu options are present. The ZOLL X Series supports 12-lead ECG monitoring when equipped and configured with the required capability. If the feature is missing from one device but present on comparable units, compare: Device configuration. Installed options. Software version. User profile. Department configuration. Do not alter protected configuration settings without authorization. Expected outcome: The 12-lead feature is confirmed as installed and accessible.

steps.title: 4. Inspect the ECG Cable and Connector
steps.instructions: Disconnect the patient before manipulating ECG accessories. Inspect the trunk cable and 12-lead lead set for: Bent, recessed, contaminated, or damaged connector pins. Cracked insulation. Cuts, stretching, or exposed conductors. Loose lead-wire connections. Fluid intrusion. Damaged snaps or clips. Strain near cable ends. Reconnect the cable firmly and verify that it seats completely. Expected outcome: The cable is secure and no external damage is identified. If reseating restores all leads, complete a functional test and stop.

steps.title: 5. Verify Electrode Placement and Contact
steps.instructions: Confirm that all required electrodes are present and correctly identified. Check for: Dried or expired electrodes. Loose electrodes. Incorrect limb or precordial placement. Hair, moisture, oil, lotion, or debris beneath electrodes. Poor skin preparation. Electrode leads connected to the wrong positions. Excessive cable tension pulling electrodes loose. Replace questionable electrodes with compatible, in-date electrodes and prepare the skin appropriately. Expected outcome: All required leads display without a lead-off indication. If acquisition becomes successful, stop after confirming print and storage functions.

steps.title: 6. Identify a Lead-Specific Failure
steps.instructions: Observe whether the device identifies a particular disconnected or unusable lead. Move or exchange only the external accessory associated with the affected lead when safe to do so. Determine whether the problem follows: The electrode. The individual lead wire. The trunk cable. The device input connection. Do not repeatedly reuse a damaged or intermittent patient cable. Expected outcome: A defective electrode, lead wire, or cable is isolated. Replace the failed accessory, perform another acquisition, and stop if the issue is resolved.

steps.title: 7. Reduce ECG Artifact
steps.instructions: If all leads are connected but the tracing is noisy: Keep the patient still when clinically possible. Support the lead wires to prevent movement. Move cables away from power cords, motors, radio transmitters, and other electrical equipment. Verify that electrodes have full skin contact. Replace dried or poorly adhering electrodes. Check whether artifact affects every lead or only one electrode group. Test the unit away from the reported location using an ECG simulator. Expected outcome: Stable waveforms are displayed and the acquisition completes without excessive artifact. Persistent artifact with a simulator and known-good cable suggests a device-side problem.

steps.title: 8. Test With Known-Good Accessories
steps.instructions: Connect a compatible, verified ECG trunk cable and lead set. Use an ECG simulator to confirm: All 12 leads are recognized. Waveforms are stable. Heart rate is displayed correctly. The acquisition completes. The report can be reviewed. The report prints when printing is configured. Expected outcome: The device acquires a complete, stable 12-lead ECG using known-good accessories. If the known-good cable resolves the failure, replace the original accessory and document its disposition.

steps.title: 9. Check Patient and Case Information
steps.instructions: Transmission workflows may require complete patient or case information. Verify that required fields are entered correctly, such as: Patient name or identifier. Incident or case number. Age or date of birth. Sex. Destination. Receiving facility. Ordering or responsible provider, when configured. Check for unsupported characters, incomplete fields, or an incorrect destination selection. Expected outcome: Required patient and destination information is accepted without validation errors.

steps.title: 10. Confirm the 12-Lead Was Saved
steps.instructions: Review the device record or 12-lead history and verify that the ECG exists locally. If the ECG is not stored: Repeat the acquisition using a simulator. Confirm that the acquisition reaches completion. Check for storage or memory warnings. Verify the device date and time. Confirm that the event or patient case remains open as required by the local workflow. Expected outcome: The completed 12-lead ECG appears in the device’s local record. If acquisition and storage work but transmission fails, continue with communication troubleshooting.

steps.title: 11. Verify the Selected Transmission Destination
steps.instructions: Confirm that the correct configured destination was selected. Compare the destination list with another functioning X Series unit from the same department. Look for: Missing destination. Incorrect facility. Obsolete destination. Duplicate destination names. Incorrect transmission method. Recently changed receiving-system configuration. Do not create or modify production destinations without approval from the appropriate Clinical Engineering, IT, or application administrator. Expected outcome: A known-valid receiving destination is selected.

steps.title: 12. Check the Wireless or Network Connection
steps.instructions: Observe the device’s communication or network indicators. Verify: Wireless communication is enabled when required. The expected network profile is selected. The device is within a known coverage area. Airplane or communication-restricted settings are not enabled. The device has not moved outside the configured network environment. Other department devices can transmit from the same location. Move the device to a location with known-good connectivity and retry the transmission. Expected outcome: The X Series connects to the expected network and displays normal communication status.

steps.title: 13. Compare the Failure by Device, Location, and Destination
steps.instructions: Perform controlled comparison testing: Same device at another location. Another X Series at the reported location. Same destination from another device. Different configured destination from the affected device, when authorized. Interpret the results: Only one device fails: suspect device configuration, network hardware, or software. Multiple devices fail in one area: suspect wireless coverage or local network service. All devices fail to one destination: suspect the receiving system or destination configuration. All transmissions fail facility-wide: escalate to IT or the application administrator. Expected outcome: The failure is narrowed to the device, network location, destination, or receiving system.

steps.title: 14. Verify Receiving-System Availability
steps.instructions: Contact the responsible IT or clinical application team and confirm whether the receiving platform is online and accepting 12-lead transmissions. ZOLL’s RescueNet 12-Lead platform is designed to receive, distribute, archive, print, and manage transmitted 12-lead ECG data. Provide: Device asset number. Device serial number. Transmission time. Patient or case identifier permitted by policy. Selected destination. Complete error message. Whether other devices are affected. Whether the ECG remains stored locally. Expected outcome: The receiving service is confirmed operational or a server-side problem is identified.

steps.title: 15. Perform a Controlled Restart
steps.instructions: After confirming that the device is not supporting a patient: Save any required case information. Power the X Series off normally. Wait briefly. Restart the device. Allow network services to initialize fully. Repeat acquisition and transmission using a simulator and test record. Expected outcome: Temporary software or communication errors clear and normal operation returns. If the restart resolves the issue, complete repeated testing before returning the device to service.

steps.title: 16. Complete an End-to-End Functional Test
steps.instructions: Before returning the device to clinical use: Connect an ECG simulator. Confirm recognition of all 12 leads. Acquire a complete 12-lead ECG. Review the tracing for stability. Print the report if configured. Save the ECG locally. Transmit it to an approved test or production destination according to facility policy. Confirm receipt with the receiving application or department. Verify correct device date and time. Clear or close the test case according to policy. Expected outcome: Acquisition, storage, printing, transmission, and receipt are all verified.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that the ZOLL X Series displayed all ECG leads but would not transmit the completed 12-lead to the emergency department destination.
CCR.Cause: The 12-lead acquired and stored normally, but the device could not connect from the reported location; transmission succeeded in an area with verified wireless coverage.
CCR.Resolution: Verified acquisition with an ECG simulator, confirmed local storage and printing, successfully transmitted from a known-good coverage area, notified IT of the location-specific network failure, and returned the device to service.

helpfulDetails: ECG cable part number and condition

title: ZOLL X Series Defibrillator - Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, Cellular, or Case Upload Failure
description: Troubleshooting wireless connection, accessory pairing, network authentication, cellular communication, or patient-case upload failures caused by external configuration and infrastructure issues.

steps.title: 1. Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Do not perform extended communication troubleshooting while the ZOLL X Series is being used to monitor, pace, cardiovert, or defibrillate a patient. If communication fails during clinical use: Confirm that monitoring, alarms, pacing, and defibrillation functions remain available. Do not delay patient care because a report, 12-lead transmission, or case upload cannot be completed. Record or retain the patient information according to facility downtime procedures. Move the patient to another verified device if the communication problem is accompanied by other equipment malfunctions. Expected outcome: Patient care continues safely without depending on wireless connectivity or successful data transmission. Continue troubleshooting only after the device is no longer supporting an active patient.

steps.title: 2. Identify the Exact Communication Failure
steps.instructions: Determine which function is affected: Wi-Fi network connection; Bluetooth accessory or device pairing; Cellular modem connection; 12-lead transmission; Case upload to ZOLL data-management software; Automatic upload after case closure; Manual upload initiated from the device. Record the complete displayed message, status icon, destination, and approximate time of the failure. Expected outcome: The affected communication path is identified before settings or network components are changed.

steps.title: 3. Confirm That the Clinical Case Is Available
steps.instructions: Open the appropriate patient-record or case-review menu and verify that: The expected case appears in device memory. The correct case is selected. The case has been ended or closed when required for upload. The case does not already show as successfully transmitted. Device storage is not reporting a full-memory or data-storage warning. If the case is missing, incomplete, or still active, correct the workflow condition and retry the upload. Expected outcome: A valid, completed case is available for transmission. If the upload succeeds, document the correction and stop.

steps.title: 4. Check the Communication Status Indicators
steps.instructions: Observe the Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, or cellular status icon and determine whether it shows: Connected; Disconnected; Searching; Disabled; Weak signal; Authentication failure; Transmission in progress; Transmission failed. Allow sufficient time for the device to complete startup and establish its configured connection. Expected outcome: The device establishes a stable connection or provides a specific failure condition for further troubleshooting.

steps.title: 5. Verify That the Required Communication Function Is Enabled
steps.instructions: Using authorized configuration access, verify that the required function is enabled: Wi-Fi radio; Bluetooth communication; Cellular modem; Automatic case upload; Manual transmission capability; Correct upload destination or server profile. Do not change protected network, destination, or security settings without authorization from the organization’s IT or ZOLL system administrator. Expected outcome: The required communication method and transmission destination are enabled. If enabling the authorized function resolves the issue, verify one successful test transmission and stop.

steps.title: 6. Check Signal Strength and Device Location
steps.instructions: Move the device to a known coverage area and verify: Adequate Wi-Fi signal; Cellular coverage; Appropriate proximity to the Bluetooth accessory; No metal enclosure, ambulance compartment, basement, elevator, or building structure is obstructing the signal. Compare performance with another known-working ZOLL X Series in the same location when available. Expected outcome: The device connects in an area with verified signal coverage. If the device works in another location, investigate wireless coverage rather than assuming equipment failure.

steps.title: 7. Inspect External Communication Hardware
steps.instructions: Inspect all accessible communication components, as equipped: Cellular modem or communication module; Antenna and antenna connection; USB or external communication accessory; Ethernet adapter or cable; Bluetooth accessory; Docking or upload interface; Protective covers surrounding communication ports. Look for: Loose connections; Bent connector pins; Damaged cables; Cracked housings; Moisture; Corrosion; Contamination; Missing accessories.
